Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zuint 0.0.0.9000

  • int64(), uint64(), int128() and uint128() create signed and unsigned 64- and 128-bit integer vectors from logical, integer, double, decimal character, bit64 integer64 and each other. Conversion is exact or gives NA with a zuint_cast_warning; it never rounds or clamps.
  • int64 has class c("zu_int64", "integer64") and bit64’s storage, so code that reads integer64 reads it unchanged.
  • NA_int64_, NA_uint64_, NA_int128_ and NA_uint128_.
  • The base vector protocol for all four types: subsetting and assignment (with exact casting of the assigned value), c(), rep(), rev(), length<-, is.na(), anyNA(), as.character(), as.double() (with a zuint_precision_warning when it rounds), as.integer(), as.logical(), as.list(), data frame columns, format(), print(), str() and summary().
  • zu_storage() and zu_from_storage() expose the raw payload.
  • Exact arithmetic: +, -, *, %/% (floor), %% (sign of the divisor), ^ with a non-negative integer exponent, unary minus, abs() and sign(). An out-of-range result is NA with one zuint_overflow_warning per call. / and other Math functions compute in double.
  • checked_add(), checked_sub(), checked_mul(), checked_pow() and checked_neg() raise a zuint_overflow_error instead, and checked_idiv() and checked_mod() a zuint_division_error on a zero divisor; wrapping_add(), wrapping_sub(), wrapping_mul(), wrapping_pow() and wrapping_neg() compute modulo 2^64 or 2^128.
  • Mixed types follow a lossless promotion order (zu_common_type()), in arithmetic and in c(). A double must be integral and in range, unless options(zuint.double = "allow").
  • Comparison is exact across all types and doubles: int64(1) == 1.5 is FALSE, and nothing is compared through double.
  • The constructors read 0x hex and 0b binary as well as decimal, with an optional sign, _ between digits and surrounding whitespace; "NA" and blank strings are NA. Exponents are not accepted.
  • format_hex() and format_bin(), with pad = TRUE for the full width; format() takes width and big.mark; print() stops at getOption("max.print").
  • Bit operations: bit_and(), bit_or(), bit_xor(), bit_not(), shift_left(), shift_right(), popcount(), clz() and ctz().
  • zu_from_arrow() and zu_to_arrow() convert through the Arrow C Data Interface with no R package in between: int64, uint64, DuckDB’s arrow.opaque hugeint/uhugeint, and decimal128(p, 0). zu_sentinel_check() counts engine values that would import as NA.
  • With nanoarrow installed, nanoarrow::convert_array(array, int64()) and the other prototypes import through the bridge, and nanoarrow::as_nanoarrow_array() exports zuint vectors.
  • zu_duckdb_query() reads DuckDB results with BIGINT, UBIGINT, HUGEINT and UHUGEINT columns as zuint vectors, exactly, and zu_duckdb_register() writes them back with their types.
  • zu_arrow_table() and zu_from_arrow_table() carry zuint columns through Arrow Tables, and so through Parquet files. With arrow loaded, arrow::as_arrow_array() and arrow::infer_type() work for int64 and uint64.
  • as_integer64() returns a plain bit64 integer64.
  • sort(), and base order() and rank() through an exact xtfrm(), with a stable radix sort; unique(), duplicated() and anyDuplicated() with an exact hash; match(), %in% and table() compare exact values, and zu_match() and %zin% do it faster.
  • sum() is type stable and exact, NA with a warning when the total does not fit; prod(), cumsum(), cumprod(), cummax() and cummin(); min(), max() and range() are exact; mean() and median() are doubles from the exact values; diff() and seq_zu().
  • summary() adds the median and the mean.
  • With vctrs, dplyr and tibble: zuint columns combine by the promotion order, cast exactly, arrange, group, summarise, bind and print. data.table keys on int64 natively.
  • zu_ifelse() and zu_vapply() keep the type where ifelse() and vapply() would read raw bits.
  • A getting-started vignette, and benchmarks against bit64 in the README.
